svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D7 — Chapter 7 · Ch07_SchauderBasesZeta, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,983 declarations of the 84 items on C7, each with its kind, file, line and state; 121 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted.

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C7's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card. First the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: Uses the sign convention for index zero from §B.5.3.2 and the Euler factors of §3.2.1, with factor one at ramified places. A positive lower bound on the reciprocal product expresses both the upper bound and avoidance of poles.

g.text: As in §3.3, the complex-place abscissae start at minus half the absolute angular weight. The union allows more than one place to contribute to the same pole.

g.text: The open strip Re z ∈ (-A, 1) includes zero and the actual archimedean abscissae (F87); the residue of (r g)⁻ᶻ Z f z fixes the Laurent sign and index (F89, I211); the character contributes its conjugate; shared poles are assigned once according to assign (F88).

g.text: Uses the Dirichlet density, written out as this limit. The limit is the body of Mathlib's NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity; the pinned Mathlib does not expose that definition and has no lemma that introduces it, so a statement phrased with the predicate itself cannot be proved outside Mathlib's own module.

text.tspan: · pp. 360–363 · 87 declarations, 4 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Uses zero-moment principal-value preimages and a nontrivial component.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Uses the intersections from (7.3.3.18)–(7.3.3.19) and a nontrivial norm-one character. At the trivial character an ambient Fourier functional restricts to zero. The pole orders use the S′-local Mellin transform and order k selects Laurent exponent −k in the signed convention of Definition 7.1.2.1.

g.text: Uses the nontrivial components of the repaired basis theorem.

g.text: Uses the intersection quotient from the proof and the same zero-extension convention as Theorem 7.3.1.6(5). The lattice is based at any pole at the chosen place.

g.text: The real and complex cutoff tuples are combined into a single place-indexed family. Local poles are ranked by positive real norm shifts, so a cutoff of n includes n + 1 local poles.

text.tspan: · p. 368 · 38 declarations, 2 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Uses the adelic tensor realization of §2.1.3 and the flat jet conditions from §5.3.3. The tensor image carries the subspace topology from the adelic Schwartz space. The display on p. 368 writes the projective tensor topology.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Implements the prose Fourier-moment condition. On a nontrivial norm-one isotype the moment restriction can be imposed on representatives, since the two polar functionals are trivial-isotypic.

g.text: Page 368 names the quasi-character |·|^(it₀). The chart parameter it₀ corresponds to the trivial quasi-character when χ = |·|^(−it₀).

g.text: Uses the Fourier-moment correction from the prose after (7.4.3.1). Without it the printed image need not be contained in the zero-moment theta space.
